sentences.text:
Opposite Party
 Coram :- Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ratnaker Bhengra

For the Petitioner :- Mr. Vishal Kumar Rai, Advocate
 For the State :- Mr. Shailesh Kr. Sinha, App
 ...
Heard both the counsels.
The petitioner is an accused in this case for the offence registered under sections 376 of the Indian Penal Code.
The learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the FIR has been lodged by the victim against this petitioner.
The petitioner happens to be the brother-in-law of the victim.
The learned counsel has further submitted that the allegations are based on land dispute that was existing between the brothers of the petitioner, therefore, the case is clearly motivated.
The learned counsel has further submitted that the charge has been framed and the stage of trial is that the witnesses are yet to be examined but no witnesses could be examined so far.
Moreover, the petitioner is in custody since 20.09.2022.
Therefore, the petitioner may be granted privilege of bail.
Learned counsel for the State has vehemently opposed the bail application of the petitioner and has submitted that the case is against her own brother-in-law.
The learned counsel has further submitted that the victim in para-44 of the case diary has supported the prosecution case.

Moreover,
in the medical report, no injury of any such kind has been indicated as she is a married lady and that the examination was done after a long time of alleged occurrence.

Having gone through the records of the case and arguments in the facts and circumstances, I am not inclined to grant bail to the present petitioner, named above, in connection with Saiko PS Case No.26 of 2022, corresponding to GR No. 613 of 2022 (ST No.229 of 2022), pending in the Court of the learned DASJ 1st at Khunti.
